explanation: High dimensional data corresponds to three-dimensional objects: In the PCA dimension reduction algorithm, high dimensional data refers to data with multiple features. In three-dimensional projection, a three-dimensional object refers to an object with three dimensions. Here, both high dimensional data and three-dimensional objects represent entities with multiple attributes.

Dimensionality reduction corresponds to mapping: The PCA dimension reduction algorithm achieves dimensionality reduction by mapping high dimensional data onto a low dimensional space. In three-dimensional projection, mapping refers to the process of projecting a three-dimensional object onto a two-dimensional plane. In this mapping, dimensionality reduction and mapping both represent the process of transformation from high dimensional to low dimensional.

Low dimensional data corresponds to two-dimensional planes: The result of the PCA dimension reduction algorithm is low dimensional data, which represents data points from the original data in the reduced space. In three-dimensional projection, a two-dimensional plane refers to the projected plane. Here, both low dimensional data and two-dimensional planes represent the results of dimension reduction or projection.

background.source: PCA Dimensionality Reduction Algorithm is a powerful technique used to reduce the dimensions of high dimensional data. It is a nonlinear method that projects high-dimensional data onto lower-dimensional latent manifolds, so that the data can be visualized or the mapping from high-dimensional space to low-dimensional embedding can be learned. The algorithm is a generalization of linear decomposition methods like singular value decomposition and principal component analysis. With the PCA technique, high-dimensional data can be reduced to low-dimensional data, making it easier to handle and analyze.
background.target: A 3D projection is a powerful design tool that allows for the depiction of three-dimensional objects on a two-dimensional surface. By breaking down an object's basic shape into a map of points, a visual representation can be created that gives the illusion of depth and dimensionality. This technique is commonly used in engineering drawing, drafting, and computer graphics. Despite being displayed on a two-dimensional medium, 3D projections allow for the interpretation of the image as representing a solid object in three dimensions. Whether using mathematical analysis or geometric and optical techniques, 3D projections offer a versatile and effective means of visualizing complex objects.
